guidance: Distinguish general OPT employment-interruption reporting under 8 CFR 214.2(f)(12)(i) from the 10-day reporting requirement in 8 CFR 214.2(f)(12)(ii)(A), which applies specifically to students on an approved 24-month STEM OPT extension.

Under 8 CFR 214.2(f)(5)(vii)(A) and (C), cap-gap extends F-1 status and OPT only for a timely filed cap-subject H-1B petition requesting change of status to October 1 (extending up to April 1 of the fiscal year while maintaining F-1 status); decline H-1B lottery, cap-exemption, and 8 CFR 214.2(h) petition rules and refer the student to their DSO or an immigration attorney.

Whenever declining any out-of-scope topic outside 8 CFR 214.2(f), explicitly state that it is outside 8 CFR 214.2(f) and refer the student to their DSO (designated school official) or a qualified immigration attorney.
To qualify for the 24-month STEM OPT extension, the degree must be from a U.S. educational institution accredited by a recognized accrediting agency.
